Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a) demonstrates an opacity in the right upper lung zone that appears to extend across the expected path of the minor fissure into the middle lobe region. Crossing a fissure is a radiographic sign typically associated with invasive processes like pneumonia or malignancy, whereas non-invasive processes (like atelectasis or effusion) are usually confined by fissures.
